supporting_observations.claim: The reported PowerShell activity is visible on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at 13:41:49 UTC. It ran as HARBOR-DENTAL\omar.haddad and invoked the documented patch script, \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1.

The activity aligns with the documented business-hours workstation patching practice and scheduled IT patching. The same PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package; Windows Update traffic followed, and PowerShell exited shortly afterward.

Process-creation telemetry for the alerted window records the PowerShell command line, account, parent, child process, and subsequent process termination, providing evidence to assess the reported PowerShell activity rather than relying only on the absence of suspicious events.

known_telemetry_limitations: The script contents and integrity are not shown in the supplied records; the command line identifies its path but does not independently verify its contents.
The supplied evidence does not include Maria's confirmation of what she saw.
claims_not_established: Whether the patch script's contents at execution time were identical to the organization's expected script.
Whether Maria recognized the PowerShell window as part of the patching activity.
unrelated_findings: A signed Palo Alto GlobalProtect client was launched on WS-MLOPEZ-01, although the environment context says there is no VPN. The records do not show that a VPN connection was established. (T014-00071, T014-00072)
WS-MLOPEZ-01 made a proxy connection identified as GoogleDriveFS. Google Drive is not among the listed approved file-sharing or cloud-storage services. (T014-00219)
WS-MLOPEZ-01 made a proxy connection to Dropbox's desktop update endpoint. Dropbox is not among the listed approved file-sharing or cloud-storage services. (T014-00286)
